{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZjVXLA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDKDj0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 83, "title": "Resolve and correct SPC700 timer live-target comparison and counter wrapping", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `4f7ab0d8b36b390a7316eb6a968e3ec86eb37418`, SPC timers use a `u16` counting stage and trigger when `stage >= target`, with target zero translated to 256. Target writes update RAM without resetting that stage. Consequently, lowering a running timer's target below its current stage causes an output increment on the next divider pulse. Whether this matches hardware has not been established. See [Apu::tick/read/write](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/4f7ab0d8b36b390a7316eb6a968e3ec86eb37418/crates/snes-core/src/apu.rs#L107).

Existing evidence does not discriminate live-target semantics: [spc_word_arithmetic_timer_and_direct_page](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/4f7ab0d8b36b390a7316eb6a968e3ec86eb37418/crates/snes-core/tests/regression.rs#L1411) uses fixed target 1; the APU cadence test uses fixed target 125. Memory's original sound driver also uses fixed targets for music and effects, making preservation of its audio regressions important. See [APU timing tests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/4f7ab0d8b36b390a7316eb6a968e3ec86eb37418/crates/snes-core/src/apu.rs#L835) and [memory-audio.py](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/4f7ab0d8b36b390a7316eb6a968e3ec86eb37418/tools/memory-audio.py).

This is the next bounded prerequisite identified by the supplied latest assessment. No open Issue is listed, and the supplied completed improvements do not address it.

## Expected outcome

Establish the documented live-target comparison and counting-stage width, then implement the smallest correction demonstrated by independent expectations and executable regressions. This is an implementation Issue with a necessary specification-reconciliation step.

### Specification prerequisite and candidate contract

Consult [nocash's Fullsnes hardware specification](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), specifically SNES APU timers and registers `$F1`, `$FA–$FC`, and `$FD–$FF`. Record the inspected revision or retrieval date, exact sections, and supporting passages. Corroborate disputed details with independently attributed hardware research where available; another emulator's behavior alone is insufficient.

The repository contains references to Fullsnes but no inspected local timer-specification text. External sources were not accessed during this repository-only planning pass. Therefore the following is a **candidate contract to reconcile, not a verified hardware finding**:

- Timers 0/1 receive counting pulses every 128 SPC clocks; timer 2 every 16.
- Each pulse increments an eight-bit counting stage modulo 256, then compares it for equality with the current eight-bit target.
- Equality clears that stage and increments the four-bit output modulo 16. Target zero therefore matches upon wrap to zero.
- Writing a target changes the comparison value without resetting the counting stage, divider phase, or accumulated output and without itself generating an event.
- Reading an output returns and clears that output, without restarting the counting stage or divider.

Explicitly resolve increment/comparison order, equality versus threshold comparison, wrap width, and target-write effects before encoding expectations. Correct this candidate contract if the sources contradict it. Do not preserve `>=`, require equality, or reset state merely because existing code or newly written tests do so.

Scope is the running timer's live-target comparator and wrap behavior, plus necessary controls. Non-goals: disabled-divider phase, `$F0` clock controls, SLEEP/STOP wake behavior, write-only register readback, warm-reset retention, physical SPC bus-access timing, coincident write/read edges, IPL execution, DSP subcycles, PAL, frontend work, and unrelated refactoring.

## Context and reproduction

Construct each stage through ordinary enabled counting, then write a target between divider pulses. Under the candidate contract above, these independently derived discriminators apply. Counts below are **divider pulses after the write**, not master clocks.

| Initial target | Stage before write | New target | Candidate first event | Current implementation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 200 | 150 | 100 | 206 pulses | 1 pulse |
| 200 | 150 | 150 | 256 pulses | 1 pulse |
| 100 | 50 | 200 | 150 pulses | 150 pulses |
| 0 | 254 | 1 | 3 pulses | 1 pulse |
| 200 | 150 | 0 | 106 pulses | 106 pulses |
| 0 | 250 | 255 | 5 pulses | 5 pulses |

For wrapping equality, the positive distance is `(new_target - stage) mod 256`, with distance zero meaning 256 pulses. These are analytical predictions, not executed baseline results or hardware captures. Revise the table if specification reconciliation establishes different semantics.

Changing only `>=` to `==` while retaining an unbounded stage is insufficient under this candidate contract: a lowered target must remain reachable after eight-bit wrap.

Use the existing firmware-free uploader pattern in [dsp_brr_end.rs](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/4f7ab0d8b36b390a7316eb6a968e3ec86eb37418/crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_brr_end.rs#L501) for original guest coverage. Guest timing windows must tolerate the existing whole-instruction execution model; they must not manufacture claims about physical access edges.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the reconciled hardware contract and authoritative source links before implementing it. Distinguish directly documented facts, derived arithmetic, and unresolved details. If the comparator/wrap dispute cannot be resolved, report that prerequisite as unresolved instead of claiming a completed correction.
- [ ] Add original tests covering all three timers: targets 1, 255, and zero; lowering below the stage; writing the current stage; raising the target; transitions to/from zero; and continuing through wrap. Check immediately before and at the supported event boundary, plus subsequent periods. Exercise target writes at more than one divider phase without relying on coincident accesses.
- [ ] Test observable output behavior: modulo-16 accumulation, read-to-clear, independence among timers, and continued counting after a read. Target writes must have the source-supported effects on stage, divider, and output. Reach test stages by counting rather than assigning fabricated internal state.
- [ ] Add `crates/snes-core/tests/spc_timers.rs` with public-API coverage and an original uploaded SPC700 guest. The guest must execute target writes and output reads itself, store independently expected results in RAM or ports, and finish within explicit instruction/master-clock or acknowledgement bounds. Include a discriminating live-target case and unchanged-target controls. Use independent timing arithmetic and windows away from unresolved access edges.
- [ ] Run the new public discriminator against the unmodified baseline and record an actual behavioral failure, then its passage after the smallest supported production correction. Do not describe an analytical prediction or compilation failure as baseline behavioral evidence.
- [ ] Compare equivalent whole and irregularly partitioned `Apu::tick` runs at fixed checkpoints, including guest records, ports, RAM, DSP registers, and PCM. Require independent timer expectations as well as equality between runs; partition equality establishes determinism only.
- [ ] Document original MIT authorship and fixture construction in [PROVENANCE.md](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/4f7ab0d8b36b390a7316eb6a968e3ec86eb37418/tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md). Use original tests or existing licensed source-built fixtures. Acquire no commercial ROM or firmware and import no emulator implementation or captured emulator output as the oracle.
- [ ] Pass the focused test and existing Rust checks:

  ```sh
  cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test spc_timers
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
  cargo test --workspace --locked
  ```

  Preserve the fixed-target timer/cadence assertions and existing BRR-end, directory, noise, pitch, envelope, mixing, and echo regressions. Do not weaken assertions to accommodate the change.

- [ ] Run the existing source-built hardware gates using the [README prerequisites](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/4f7ab0d8b36b390a7316eb6a968e3ec86eb37418/README.md#validate):

  ```sh
  python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
  python3 tools/hardware-tests.py \
    --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" \
    --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" \
    --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
  python3 tools/ppu-test.py \
    --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
  ```

- [ ] Preserve fixture reproducibility and mandatory browser/game regressions:

  ```sh
  python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
  cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
  python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
  python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
  npm --prefix web ci
  npm --prefix web run build
  npm --prefix web exec -- playwright install chromium
  npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
  ```

  Retain source pins, expected game hashes, Castle replays/progression, Memory music-note durations and finite effects, and gesture-activated Web Audio checks. The filter excludes existing optional unaudited tests; it must not exclude the mandatory cleared-game checks. Follow README toolchain overrides where required.

- [ ] Report commands, actual results, baseline failures, and any skipped checks accurately. Update timer limitations without claiming full SPC accuracy, commercial compatibility, or Issue #3 completion.

### Inventory continuity and remaining work

Retain every supplied inventory category, its full scope, and outstanding work. All remain **partial** except `ppu-raster` and `pal`, which remain **unimplemented**; none becomes verified:

`cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-hires`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-raster`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-voices`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo`, `dsp-timing`, `pal`.

For `spc`, this Issue addresses only supported live-target/comparator/wrap corrections. Disabled-divider phase, physical instruction/access timing, communication races, SLEEP/STOP differences, register readback, reset retention, and comprehensive instruction semantics remain unresolved or incompletely tested. Preserve the supplied assessment's corrections to stale historical inventory descriptions, including implemented EXTBG and selected hidden-envelope behavior.

Planning evidence: HEAD matched the supplied baseline and the working tree was clean. Code, tests, contribution guidance, provenance, and validation commands were inspected read-only. No suites were rerun, external specifications retrieved, files changed, or remote actions taken.

## Optional validation

None required. Independently sourced physical measurements may strengthen the specification record but are not a mandatory hardware-access or human-approval gate.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
